records.description: The Beas meets the Sutlej near Harike. NCERT identifies the Panjnad as the combined waters of the Sutlej, Beas, Ravi, Chenab and Jhelum in the Indus system.
records.referenceDate: NCERT India: Physical Environment, Chapter 3, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Major river tributaries and drainage connections
records.description: The Alaknanda system includes the Dhauli and Vishnu Ganga, with the Pindar joining at Karna Prayag and the Mandakini (Kali Ganga) joining at Rudra Prayag.
records.referenceDate: NCERT India: Physical Environment, Chapter 3, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Major river tributaries and drainage connections
records.description: Yamuna tributaries include Chambal, Sind, Betwa and Ken on the right bank, and Hindan, Rind, Sengar and Varuna on the left. Ramganga and Gomati are also Ganga tributaries.
records.referenceDate: NCERT India: Physical Environment, Chapter 3, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Major river tributaries and drainage connections
records.description: Major Ganga tributaries entering or flowing through Bihar include the Son, Ghaghara, Gandak, Kosi and Mahananda.
records.referenceDate: NCERT India: Physical Environment, Chapter 3, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Major river tributaries and drainage connections
records.description: The Mahananda is a left-bank tributary of the Ganga in West Bengal. The Damodar joins the Hugli; Barakar is the main tributary of the Damodar.
records.referenceDate: NCERT India: Physical Environment, Chapter 3, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Major river tributaries and drainage connections
records.description: The Barakar is the main tributary of the Damodar, which flows along the eastern margins of the Chota Nagpur Plateau.
records.referenceDate: NCERT India: Physical Environment, Chapter 3, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Major river tributaries and drainage connections
records.description: The Chambal rises near Mhow in Madhya Pradesh, flows through Rajasthan including the Kota region, and finally joins the Yamuna.
records.referenceDate: NCERT India: Physical Environment, Chapter 3, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Major river tributaries and drainage connections
records.description: The Chambal, Sind, Betwa and Ken are Yamuna tributaries; the Son rises in the Amarkantak Plateau and joins the Ganga.
records.referenceDate: NCERT India: Physical Environment, Chapter 3, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Major river tributaries and drainage connections
records.description: Godavari tributaries include Penganga, Wainganga, Wardha (together forming Pranhita), Indravati, Sabari and Manjra. Krishna tributaries include Koyna, Ghatprabha, Malprabha and Bhima.
records.referenceDate: NCERT India: Physical Environment, Chapter 3, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Major river tributaries and drainage connections
records.description: The Manjira and Pranahita systems feed the Godavari; the Bhima and Tungabhadra are tributaries of the Krishna system. The NCERT text notes shared river systems across Telangana and neighbouring States.
records.referenceDate: NCERT India: Physical Environment, Chapter 3, 2026-27 reprint

records.name: Major river tributaries and drainage connections
records.description: Krishna tributaries include Ghataprabha, Malaprabha, Bhima and Tungabhadra. Kaveri tributaries include Hemavati, Shimsha, Arkavathy, Kabini, Bhavani, Noyyal and Amaravati.
